newsitem.title: UK: Quiet Eurobonds see rare Polish zloty offering.
newsitem.headline: Quiet Eurobonds see rare Polish zloty offering.

text.p: New issue activity was subdued on Friday, with many investors expected to stay sidelined into next week.

Japanese investors will be out of action due to the "Golden Week" holiday, which ends on May 5. Other players are expected to stay on the sidelines due to the release of U.S. economic data, which will be closely watched for signs of a build-up of inflation in the U.S.
"The U.S. data will keep most people out of the market," a syndicate manager at a U.S. bank said.
The U.S. Treasury market remained idle in London as dealers waited to find direction in next week's data.
The first quarter Employment Cost Index (ECI) is due on Tuesday, GDP data on Wednesday and non-farm payroll figures for April on Friday.
The market did see a rare Polish zloty-linked deal surface on Friday. The high-yielding zloty is not convertible, and zloty bonds are therefore payable in a different currency.
Last year, a handful of deals were launched linked to the dollar, but Friday's issue was the first linked to the mark.

Metro Finance BV, a unit of Metro AG, raised 100 million zlotys with a three-year bond which paid an 18.50 percent coupon. All payments will be made in marks at the prevailing zloty/mark exchange rate.
Lead manager Goldman Sachs was not immediately available for comment.
Elsewhere, Poland's Bank Handlowy was holding investor presentations in London on Friday ahead of its planned $200 million Eurobond.
The deal, to be lead managed by J.P. Morgan, will have a three- or five-year maturity and is expected to be launched next week.
